vo: Excluded from testing. Still on the cert.
Myth: if a testing exclusion applies, the rule comes off the certificate.
It stays listed. In place of the test date and place, the cert names the exclusion.
Say yours just drops the rule. That's a gap, even with no test needed.
Blocked right now? Forward the notice. Get your gap list in twenty-four hours.
caption:
No test needed doesn't mean the rule comes off the certificate.
Under 16 CFR 1110.11(c), when a certifier claims a statutory or regulatory testing exclusion, the certificate still lists every applicable rule.
For that rule, it identifies the exclusion in place of the date and place of testing.
Leaving the rule off is a gap, even when no test was required.

sources.claim: Testing exclusion: rule still listed, exclusion named instead of test date/place
sources.quote: if a finished product certifier is claiming a statutory or regulatory testing exclusion to an applicable consumer product safety rule or similar rule, ban, standard, or regulation, then in addition to listing all applicable rules, bans, standards, and regulations as required under § 1110.11(a)(2), and in lieu of providing the date and place where testing was conducted for that regulation under § 1110.11(a)(6), a finished product certificate shall identify the applicable testing exclusion.
